score_basis: Non-statistical internal evidence-quality score based on adopted London fire policy, current government/HSE Planning Gateway One guidance and explicit future-effective-date handling for 2026 Approved Document B amendments.

sources.label: London Plan 2021 Policy D12 Fire safety
sources.fact: Adopted policy requires all development proposals to achieve the highest standards of fire safety, including evacuation, fire-appliance access and firefighting provision.

sources.label: London Plan 2021 Policy D5 Inclusive design
sources.fact: Where lifts are installed, at least one suitably sized evacuation lift per core is required as a minimum, subject to capacity assessment.

sources.label: GLA statement on fire safety and tall buildings
sources.fact: The 2023 GLA statement required two staircases for referred residential buildings over 30m as an interim planning position; it is retained as dated London planning evidence rather than current national Building Regulations threshold.

sources.label: GLA Fire Safety Guidance pre-consultation information
sources.fact: The page identifies D12, D5 evacuation-lift and fire-statement documents as pre-consultation drafts/information and therefore not final adopted guidance.

sources.label: Fire Safety LPG 2022 consultation
sources.fact: Consultation material explains major developments must submit a Fire Statement under D12 and developments with a lift core need evacuation-lift provision under D5; consultation status is retained.

sources.label: Approved Document B Fire safety
sources.fact: Current GOV.UK collection provides Approved Document B volumes and collates 2025, 2026 and future 2029 amendments with transitional arrangements.

sources.label: 2026 Approved Document B amendment
sources.fact: Second-stair provisions for residential buildings over 18m come into force on 30 September 2026 subject to transitional provisions; on 27 July 2026 this is FUTURE_EFFECTIVE_DATE evidence and is not applied early.

sources.label: Planning Gateway One current guidance
sources.fact: Relevant buildings for Planning Gateway One contain two or more dwellings/educational accommodation and are 18m+ or 7+ storeys; relevant applications generally require a fire statement.

sources.label: Planning Gateway One fire statement scope
sources.fact: Fire statements cover planning-stage fire matters including site layout, emergency access and water supply; whole-development information is required where relevant.

sources.label: Planning fire statement versus Building Regulations
sources.fact: Planning fire statements address land-use planning matters and do not duplicate or establish compliance with Building Regulations or the Fire Safety Order.

sources.label: HSE fire safety and planning
sources.fact: HSE is a statutory consultee for planning applications that involve or may involve a relevant building and offers pre-application advice on planning-stage fire matters.

sources.label: Building Safety Regulator Planning Gateway One review
sources.fact: Official Building Safety Regulator material reiterates the 18m/7-storey relevant-building threshold and early integration of fire safety into planning/design.

examples.result: D12 is retained as adopted planning policy but is not treated as Building Regulations approval.
D5 evacuation-lift requirement is kept distinct from firefighters-lift/building-control requirements.
GLA 2023 over-30m two-stair statement is date-tagged historical/interim evidence and not substituted for the future national 18m rule.
30 September 2026 second-stair amendment is FUTURE_EFFECTIVE_DATE on 27 July 2026 and is not applied early.
Planning Gateway One 18m/7-storey threshold is checked against actual proposed building form, not parcel area.
A planning fire statement does not prove Building Regulations compliance or Building Safety Regulator approval.
HSE statutory-consultee status does not imply approval unless an actual consultation response/application is evidenced.
No fire/building-safety promotion occurs without exact proposal height/storeys/use, fire strategy and current regulatory evidence.
